Article Title: Bankipur assembly bypoll: 'Nitish Kumar', 'Lalu Prasad Yadav' lose security deposits
Article Text:
Polling for Bankipur assembly byelection was held on July 30 (Representative photo)

Independent candidates Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav polled 149 and 81 votes respectively

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: While the spotlight is on Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor , who emerged victorious in his very first electoral outing by wresting BJP bastion Bankipur from the saffron party, "Nitish Kumar" and " Lalu Prasad Yadav " were not as fortunate.The namesakes of Bihar's two political stalwarts and former chief ministers failed to make an impact. The duo, who contested as independents, secured fewer than 150 votes each and lost their deposits.While Lalu Prasad Yadav secured just 81 votes, accounting for a vote share of 0.06%, Nitish Kumar performed slightly better with 149 votes, translating into 0.11% of the total votes polled.They lost their security deposits as per Election Commission rules, which stipulate that candidates who fail to secure at least one-sixth of the total valid votes polled forfeit their deposits, which are then transferred to the treasury.A total of 25 candidates contested the seat, including eight independents.The defeat of the namesakes of Bihar's two political heavyweights came at a time when both leaders are away from active electoral politics. Nitish Kumar resigned as chief minister in March after over two decades in office and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha, while Lalu Prasad Yadav, who has been battling health issues, cannot contest elections and remains barred from holding public office following his conviction in the fodder scam cases.Prashant Kishor defeated Neeraj Kumar, a BJP youth wing leader who was hurriedly fielded by the ruling party after its candidate Abhishek "Bunty" withdrew from the contest at the eleventh hour, citing "family reasons".The former election strategist polled 64,151 votes, defeating Neeraj Kumar by a margin of 19,324 votes. RJD's Rekha Gupta, coincidentally a namesake of BJP leader and Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, finished a distant third with 14,273 votes.The bypoll was necessitated after BJP chief Nitin Nabin resigned following his election to the Rajya Sabha. Nabin had won all four assembly elections from the Bankipur seat since it was created in 2008.The Bankipur assembly constituency, which has nearly 3.8 lakh voters, recorded a turnout of 34.30% in polling held on July 30, significantly lower than the 41.45% turnout recorded in the 2025 Assembly election. The votes were counted on Monday.
Article Summary: The namesakes of Bihar's two political stalwarts failed to make an impact. Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad Yadav secured fewer than 150 votes each and lost their deposits. Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor emerged victorious in his first electoral outing.

Article Title: NEET (UG) protests: Gujarat latest BJP-ruled state to order withdrawal of FIRs against demonstrators
Article Text:
Protests were held in various cities of Gujarat seeking the resignation of then education minister Dhrmendra Pradhan (PTI photo)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat government has directed the state police to withdraw all criminal cases registered against students, youths and others who took part in recent protests over the alleged NEET-UG examination paper leak, officials said on Monday.With this, Gujarat has become the latest BJP-ruled state to withdraw FIRs against NEET protesters. Similar decisions have already been taken by the BJP governments in Assam, Bihar, Delhi and Maharashtra.In a July 31 letter to the state's Director General of Police GS Malik, the Gujarat home department cited the Supreme Court's July 28 judgment restraining police from taking coercive action against minor student protesters and directed the immediate withdrawal of all existing cases.The department instructed the police not to initiate any adverse legal or penal action against individuals who participated in the protests in the state. It further directed that if any FIRs or criminal cases had already been registered against protesters, the legal process for their withdrawal should be completed immediately.The communication, however, did not specify how many FIRs or criminal cases would be withdrawn.Protests were held in Gujarat's Ahmedabad and several other cities in support of demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical outfit that had been leading an indefinite sit-in at Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its protest on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Besides seeking Pradhan's resignation, the CJP had demanded that no action be taken against its members or any NEET protesters across the country.The CJP has repeatedly warned that it would resume its agitation if the FIRs are not withdrawn.Meanwhile, the Supreme Court also clarified on Monday that the expression "criminal antecedents" in its July 28 order on releasing student protesters referred only to those involved in grave and heinous offences, and said states could close or withdraw FIRs against the remaining students in accordance with law.
Article Summary: Gujarat has become the latest BJP-ruled state to withdraw FIRs against NEET protesters. Similar decisions have already been taken by the BJP governments in Assam, Bihar, Delhi and Maharashtra. Supreme Court also clarified on Monday that the expression "criminal antecedents" in its July 28 order on releasing student protesters referred only to those involved in grave and heinous offences.

Article Title: 'Entire system working to protect Brij Bhushan': Vinesh Phogat says wrestlers to continue fight

Phogat accused the authorities of shielding the former BJP MP throughout the case

NEW DELHI: Wrestler Vinesh Phogat said the women wrestlers would appeal against the acquittal of former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh . She alleged that "the entire state machinery, the government, and the system have been working to protect Brij Bhushan" since the beginning of the case.In a statement issued after the verdict on Monday, Phogat accused the authorities of shielding the former BJP MP throughout the case and confirmed that the wrestlers had instructed their lawyers to appeal."We had to muster a great deal of courage to take to the streets and get an FIR registered against a powerful leader of the ruling party. Using the influence of the government and his own political clout, Brij Bhushan intimidated several girls into withdrawing their names from the case. Yet, several women wrestlers stood firm and continued fighting against Brij Bhushan in court," she wrote.Expressing disappointment over the verdict, Phogat said, "We are deeply saddened that the court did not find Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh guilty of the sexual harassment allegations brought by the women wrestlers."She went on to allege that, "From the very beginning, the entire state machinery, the government, and the system have been working to protect Brij Bhushan."Announcing the next legal step, Phogat added, "The women wrestlers have instructed their lawyers to appeal against this verdict, and the appeal will be filed as soon as possible. We have not lost hope, and the wrestlers will continue their fight."The statement came hours after Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwini Panwar acquitted Singh and co-accused Vinod Tomar, the former WFI assistant secretary, in the sexual harassment case filed by six women wrestlers.Speaking to reporters outside the court, Singh welcomed the verdict, calling it an "honourable" acquittal."On the first day, I had said that if any allegation against me was proved, I would hang myself. The court has now honourably acquitted me. I am happy and grateful to my lawyers," he said, adding that he would comment further after reading the detailed order.The court had reserved its verdict on July 2 after hearing final arguments. The Delhi Police had filed a chargesheet against Brij Bhushan in June 2023 under provisions of the Indian Penal Code relating to sexual harassment, stalking, criminal intimidation and assault or criminal force intended to outrage the modesty of a woman.
Article Summary: Wrestler Vinesh Phogat said the women wrestlers would appeal against the acquittal of former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. She accused the authorities of shielding the former BJP MP throughout the case. Singh welcomed the verdict, calling it an "honourable" acquittal.

Article Title: BJP retains Manjalpur seat as Satish Patel defeats Congress by over 30,000 votes
Article Text:
Satish Patel won the contest by a margin of 30,630 votes.





VADODARA: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday retained the Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat's Vadodara district, with its candidate Satish Patel defeating Congress nominee Bhikhabhai Rabari by a margin of more than 30,000 votes in the by-election.According to Election Commission data, Satish Patel secured 55,481 votes, while Rabari received 24,851 votes after the completion of all 20 rounds of counting, according to news agency PTI.Patel won the contest by a margin of 30,630 votes.The counting process began at 8 am at Bhavan's School in Vadodara's Makarpura area under tight security arrangements.The by-election, held on July 30, recorded a voter turnout of 37.5 per cent.The seat fell vacant following the death of senior BJP MLA and former Gujarat minister Yogesh Patel on June 2 after a prolonged illness, necessitating the bypoll.For the contest, the BJP fielded former Vadodara Municipal Corporation councillor Satish Govindbhai Patel, while the Congress nominated its Gujarat vice-president and former minister Bhikhabhai Rabari.The election witnessed a direct contest between the two candidates.With the victory, the BJP's tally in the 182-member Gujarat Assembly has increased to 162.The Congress now has 12 MLAs, while the Aam Aadmi Party holds five seats. The remaining members include two Independents and one Samajwadi Party legislator.
Article Summary: Satish Patel secured 55,481 votes, while Bhikhabhai Rabari received 24,851 votes. The seat fell vacant following the death of senior BJP MLA and former Gujarat minister Yogesh Patel on June 2. The counting process began at 8 am at Bhavan's School in Vadodara's Makarpura area.

Article Title: Complaint filed against MP Pappu Yadav over Parliament protest on Ram Mandir donation 'theft' row
Article Text:
Complaint filed against Purnia MP Pappu Yadav in Delhi over Parliament protest





NEW DELHI: A complaint has been filed against Independent Purnia MP Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav at Delhi's Jehangirpuri Police Station over his protest inside the Parliament complex on the alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement issue, as reported by news agency ANI.The complaint, lodged by Surya Maithil, accuses Yadav of hurting religious sentiments during the demonstration. Maithil also alleged that several INDIA bloc MPs backed the protest.Claiming that Yadav insulted religious symbols, Maithil said, "The way Pappu Yadav insulted the saffron today and staged the drama outside Parliament, supported by Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Awadhesh Kumar and other INDIA alliance MPs, has hurt the sentiments of Sanatanis. During the protest, he even placed a picture of Lord Ram Lalla Virajman under his feet."He said he had sought immediate legal action against Yadav and others, urging Union home minister Amit Shah , the Delhi Police commissioner and other senior police officials to act on the complaint.On Thursday, the Parliament complex witnessed an unusual opposition protest in the form of a street play over the alleged Ram Mandir donation "theft" row.Opposition MPs also demanded that Amit Shah address Parliament over the recent police action against protesting students.Amid slogans of "Chanda chor, gaddi chhod", "Jawab tumko dena hoga" and "Amit Shah, sadan mein aao", Pappu Yadav, dressed as a temple priest in saffron robes, carried a photograph of Lord Ram and enacted a symbolic performance. As fellow opposition MPs, playing devotees, dropped donations into a collection box, Yadav was shown pocketing the money instead, before another MP confronted him in the staged act.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Complaint filed against Purnia MP Pappu Yadav in Delhi over Parliament protest. Yadav dressed as a temple priest in saffron robes and enacted a symbolic performance. As fellow opposition MPs dropped donations into a collection box, Yadav was shown pocketing the money.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquitted in sexual harassment case
Article Text:
Delhi court has acquitted former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh

‘Complainants repeatedly changed their statements’





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court Monday acquitted BJP ex-MP and former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers. Suspended WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was also acquitted.Additional chief judicial magistrate Ashwini Panwar pronounced the verdict during in-camera proceedings. The detailed order is awaited.The trial concluded nearly three years after Delhi Police filed its chargesheet against Singh, during which the court examined 32 prosecution witnesses. Of the six complainants, two later turned hostile, while charges were not framed in relation to the allegations of the third complainant.Public prosecutor Manish Rawat told TOI, “We will get the judgment tomorrow. We will examine it and take appropriate steps before higher courts accordingly.”The case arose from complaints by several women wrestlers alleging Singh sexually harassed them between 2016 and 2019 at WFI office, his official residence and on foreign trips. The charges triggered months-long protests in New Delhi in 2023 by prominent wrestlers, including Sakshi Malik, Vinesh Phogat, Bajrang Punia and Sangeeta Phogat, demanding Singh’s arrest.Following SC’s intervention in May 2023, Delhi Police registered an FIR against Singh. The Union sports ministry constituted an oversight committee to conduct an internal probe. On June 15, 2023, police filed a chargesheet against Singh under sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment, including sexually coloured remarks), 354D (stalking) and 506(1) (criminal intimidation) of IPC. Tomar was booked under Section 109 (abetment).On May 10, 2024, the trial court framed charges of sexual harassment and outraging the modesty of women against Singh in connection with the complaints of five women wrestlers, while discharging him in the complaint of the sixth wrestler. Tomar was charged under section 506(1) for alleged criminal intimidation in connection with one complainant and discharged from the remaining allegations.In May 2025, another Delhi court accepted a closure report filed by police in the complaint of a wrestler who was a minor when she made the allegations, after cops said they found “no corroborative evidence”.During the in-camera trial, the defence argued the complainants repeatedly changed their statements by altering the dates and locations of the alleged incidents, also highlighting the delay in lodging the complaints, arguing that some allegations related to incidents that were seven to eight years old. The prosecution, however, maintained that the victims’ statements remained consistent.Reacting to the verdict outside Rouse Avenue Court, Singh said: “I said on the very first day that if the allegations are true, I will hang myself. I am very happy that I have been acquitted today. It is good news for me and good news for my supporters.”
Article Summary: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh acquitted in sexual harassment case filed by women wrestlers. Suspended WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was also acquitted. The case arose from complaints by several women wrestlers alleging Singh sexually harassed them between 2016 and 2019.

Article Title: ‘Quit BJP, we’ll back you as 1st woman Maha CM’
Article Text: Nagpur: Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar, while reacting to BJP minister Pankaja Munde 's remarks about being tired of politics, on Monday offered her support for CM's post, on condition that she quit BJP.A video of Munde speaking at a public rally has gone viral, in which she is allegedly expressing frustration over certain things in politics and talking about wanting to retire."Our request to Pankaja tai, as an OBC leader, is that you should not take such a step. Lead OBCs and become the first woman OBC chief minister of Maharashtra," Wadettiwar said and added, "If she leaves BJP then we will request our high command to induct her into the party," he said.Blaming BJP for sidelining OBC politicians like Munde, Wadettiwar said, "OBC members have left (the party), they must be feeling that we are not getting justice, that all our sacrifices are not valued in BJP. Maybe Pankaja tai said this out of anger. Sometimes these feelings come easily when the trouble increases."Wadettiwar clarified the offer for Munde to join Congress was a personal appeal, not a formal decision."I do not have that authority. But yes, I will speak to my party seniors and request that she be brought into the Congress fold after quitting BJP," he said.He alleged the BJP-led govt had assumed office on OBC votes but ignored their legislators and voters alike. Wadettiwar made the remarks in Nagpur, before leaving for Bhandara to launch the Mandal Janganana Yatra, a campaign for a caste census of OBCs.
Article Summary: Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar offered Pankaja Munde support for CM's post, on condition that she quit BJP. A video of Munde speaking at a public rally has gone viral. She is allegedly expressing frustration over certain things in politics and talking about wanting to retire.

Article Title: 3.3 lakh party agents on paper, but BLOs say SIR burden largely theirs
Article Text:
Locating voters and their exact addresses has become a task for BLOs

Pune:





When a BLO in Pune’s Ambegaon assembly constituency tried tracing a woman voter whose surname had changed after marriage and whose address in the 2002 electoral roll no longer matched her present residence, the official expected help from the party-appointed booth-level agent. Instead, the BLO said neighbours and local residents helped locate the family.Similar experiences have been reported by several BLOs across Maharashtra who said SIR legwork could have been less taxing if political parties and their BLAs had pitched in.The state has 3,29,919 BLAs for 1,00,253 polling stations, with BJP accounting for the largest share at 94,888, followed by Shiv Sena with 69,163, Congress with 52,543, Shiv Sena (UBT) with 43,989, NCP (SP) with 26,102 and NCP with 17,425 agents.BLAs can trace voters who have moved, locate houses with incomplete addresses and identify women whose surnames changed after marriage—issues that have emerged repeatedly during the revision exercise. “Local party workers usually know where families have moved or whether an elector is still residing in the area. But during door-to-door verification, we rarely found BLAs helping us,” a BLO from Pune said.Another BLO from Pimpri Chinchwad said repeated visits to locked houses and tracing absent-shifted-deceased voters consumed much of last month.“Neighbours helped us more than party agents. Had BLAs been more involved, several discrepancies could have been resolved faster,” the official said.The contrast is striking in Pune district. Against 8,417 polling stations, political parties have appointed 27,334 BLAs, including 7,916 from BJP, 6,207 from NCP (SP), 3,866 from Shiv Sena, 3,355 from NCP, 2,778 from Shiv Sena (UBT) and 2,276 from Congress.The highest concentration of BLAs is in Mumbai Suburban (28,746), followed by Pune (27,334), Jalgaon (18,702), Nashik (18,091), Thane (16,766), Ahmednagar (13,456) and Nagpur (13,069).The effectiveness of the state’s largest-ever political booth network is expected to come under greater scrutiny as parties begin challenging additions and deletions after the draft electoral rolls are published.
Article Summary: The state has 3,29,919 BLAs for 1,00,253 polling stations, with BJP accounting for the largest share at 94,888. The highest concentration of BLAs is in Mumbai Suburban (28,746), followed by Pune (27,334)

Article Title: DMK workers protest Udhayanidhi Stalin's detention, Pudukkottai MLA among those detained
Article Text:
Protests erupted in Tamil Nadu after Udhayanidhi Stalin's detention over alleged remarks





CHENNAI: Protests erupted in parts of Tamil Nadu on Tuesday after DMK leader and Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin was detained by Chennai Police in connection with a case over his alleged remarks made during a rally on the Cauvery water dispute In the latest development, DMK cadres took to the streets in Pudukkottai, where police detained several party workers, including Pudukkottai MLA V Muthuraja, during the demonstration.Similarly, in Karur, DMK members, including Aravakurchi MLA R Elango, were also detained during protests against Udhayanidhi Stalin's detention.In Pudukkottai district's Alangudi, DMK MLA Meyyanathan Siva was also detained by police during the protests.The protest was organised against Udhayanidhi's detention from his residence in Neelankarai.Visuals from Pudukkottai showed DMK workers raising slogans and marching in protest before police intervened and detained the demonstrators.Earlier on Tuesday, a police team led by Joint Commissioner of Police Dr P Vijayakumar took Udhayanidhi into custody from his residence for questioning after an FIR was registered against him over his allegedly objectionable remarks made at a DMK rally in Thanjavur.The detention came even as Udhayanidhi approached the Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail, apprehending arrest in the case.When the matter was mentioned before Justice G K Ilanthiraiyan, the court agreed to hear the urgent plea and orally directed the police not to precipitate the issue until the petition was taken up.The controversy stems from a speech delivered by Udhayanidhi at a rally in Thanjavur on Monday during a protest over the Cauvery water-sharing dispute.Opposition parties alleged that he made objectionable remarks targeting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay.Based on a complaint filed by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), Thanjavur police registered an FIR against Udhayanidhi under charges of promoting enmity between groups, provisions of the Information Technology Act, and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.TVK also moved the National Commission for Women (NCW), alleging that Udhayanidhi's remarks were "vulgar", "objectifying" and "sexually suggestive".The party sought legal action, an unconditional public apology and intervention by the commission.TVK national spokesperson Pazha Selvakumar alleged that the remarks objectified women, undermined their dignity and lowered the standards of political discourse.
Article Summary: DMK cadres took to the streets in Pudukkottai, where police detained several party workers. In Karur, DMK members, including Aravakurchi MLA R Elango, were also detained during protests against Udhayanidhi Stalin's detention.

Article Title: Case registered against Udhayanidhi; TVK calls statewide protests, security beefed up outside MLA's house
Article Text:
Security tightened outside Udhayanidhi’s residence in Neelankarai, Chennai.





CHENNAI/TIRUCHI: Thanjavur police on Tuesday registered a case against former deputy chief minister and MLA Udayanidhi Stalin following a complaint that he made derogatory remarks about women during a protest held in Thanjavur on Monday.The case was registered based on a complaint lodged by the women’s wing organiser of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). Police said an investigation was under way.Following the registration of the case and the controversy over the speech, security was tightened outside Udayanidhi’s residence at Neelankarai in Chennai.Police deployed additional personnel in the area as a precautionary measure.Sources said Udayanidhi remained in Thanjavur on Tuesday.The remarks also triggered political reactions, with state ministers Anand, Raj Mohan, Keerthana and Venkataraman criticising the speech.Anand appealed to TVK members to participate in statewide protests organised by the party on Tuesday condemning Udayanidhi’s remarks.Police said the contents of the speech and other evidence submitted with the complaint would be examined as part of the investigation.Further action will be taken based on the outcome of the inquiry.
Article Summary: Former deputy chief minister and MLA Udayanidhi made derogatory remarks about women during a protest held in Thanjavur on Monday. The case was registered based on a complaint lodged by the women’s wing organiser of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam. Police said an investigation was under way.

Article Title: Udhayanidhi Stalin moves Madras HC for anticipatory bail over 'vulgar' remarks
Article Text:
TVK urged the NCW to take formal cognizance of the speech and video footage from the rally and take legal action for "public obscenity and outraging the modesty of women".





CHENNAI: A day after facing backlash over his allegedly objectionable remarks targeting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay during a rally on the Cauvery water dispute, DMK leader and leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Tuesday moved the Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail in the case registered against him.When Justice G K Ilanthiraiyan commenced proceedings on Tuesday, advocate Hasan Mohammed Jinnah sought an urgent hearing of the plea. Accepting the request, the judge agreed to hear the anticipatory bail petition later in the afternoon.The case stems from a DMK rally held in Thanjavur on Monday to protest the Cauvery water-sharing issue. During his address, Udhayanidhi allegedly made a double-entendre remark targeting the chief minister, triggering a political storm.Following a complaint by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), Thanjavur police registered an FIR against the DMK leader. Apprehending arrest, Udhayanidhi approached the high court for anticipatory bail.The controversy also reached the National Commission for Women (NCW), with TVK filing a complaint alleging that Udhayanidhi made "vulgar", "objectifying" and "sexually suggestive" remarks. TVK national spokesperson Pazha Selvakumar urged the commission to take cognisance of the speech, seek an explanation and an unconditional public apology, and direct authorities to initiate legal proceedings under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.According to the complaint, the remarks were made while Udhayanidhi was responding to slogans raised by party workers during the rally. TVK alleged that the comments objectified women, undermined the dignity of women in public life and lowered the standards of political discourse. The party also urged the NCW to examine the video footage of the speech and recommend legal action for alleged public obscenity and outraging the modesty of women.
Article Summary: DMK leader and leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin moved the Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail in the case registered against him. The case stems from a DMK rally held in Thanjavur on Monday to protest the Cauvery water- sharing issue. During his address, Udhayanidhi allegedly made a double-entendre remark targeting the chief minister.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Kerala HC criticises S Sreejith’s promotion as DGP
Article Text:
ADGP S Sreejith

Kochi

:





The high court, on Monday, orally criticised the state govt for promoting ADGP S Sreejith to the rank of DGP without obtaining vigilance clearance, particularly when two matters relating to vigilance inquiries against him are pending consideration.Justice A Badharudeen made the observation while hearing a petition filed by K M Shajahan of Thiruvananthapuram challenging the appointment of bodybuilders Shinu Chova and Chitharesh Natesan as inspectors in Kerala Police. During the hearing, counsel for the petitioner submitted that the state govt had promoted Sreejith even though the vigilance department was yet to decide on granting prior approval under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018, in the present case, in which he is also a party respondent. It was further contended that the promotion was made in haste soon after the retirement of fire and rescue services chief Nithin Agarwal.At the previous hearing, the state govt had sought two weeks to consider the grant of prior approval under Section 17A. The court had accordingly directed the principal secretary to decide within two weeks. The petitioner submitted that, instead of deciding on the issue, the state govt had promoted Sreejith.The court orally observed that vigilance clearance was necessary for such a promotion. It also noted that there were two orders directing the home department to consider the allegations against Sreejith — one in the present case and another relating to allegations that he had attended a private function abroad in a police uniform. In the face of such pending allegations, the authorities were duty-bound to obtain vigilance clearance before effecting the promotion, the court orally observed.The court further observed that if the promotion had been made in violation of the applicable procedure, it was open to an aggrieved person to challenge it in accordance with law. Meanwhile, in the matter relating to the appointment of the two bodybuilders, the court declined the state govt’s request for a further two weeks to consider the grant of prior approval under Section 17A and directed it to take a decision on or before Aug 10.
Article Summary: The high court orally criticised the state govt for promoting ADGP S Sreejith to the rank of DGP without obtaining vigilance clearance. The court orally observed that vigilance clearance was necessary for such a promotion. It was further contended that the promotion was made in haste soon after the retirement of fire and rescue services chief Nithin Agarwal.
